purpose: Build an animation video ad from start to finish for any product or service (line 3: "script modeled on 37 winning animation ads, voiceover first, then characters and storyboards timed to the audio, MiniMax H3 clips, final edit"). The ad is treated as "a sales letter read by a voice, with a picture for every line" (line 8). Order: Hook Lab, then Script Lab, then ElevenLabs voice, music and SFX, then audio timing, then the shot ledger, sheets, storyboards, H3 clips and the ffmpeg edit in the Higgsfield sandbox. There are 7 human GATEs and 10 hard gates. The skill is paid-only (Meta cold ads): the offer, guarantee and urgency rungs, the end card offer, CPA-based reads and a Meta ad-review check are all built in. The hub (readymerce-ads-machine G8) also points every module to this skill's Phase 5 for voice method and vo_build2.py.

phases.name: Hard gates (they cost money)
phases.does: 10 standing rules. 1: MiniMax H3 at 2K for every clip (reference mode when a mouth moves, keyframe mode otherwise). Kling 3.0 only as a fallback; never Seedance or FLUX 3; realistic humans are H3 clips from GPT Image 2 stills; sheets and storyboards on Nano Banana 2. 2: audio first. 3: one voice per character. 4: budget preflight. 5: no filler clips. 6: script released by Script Lab first. 7: look before you cut. 8: natural voice speed and a pilot. 9: Hook Lab first. 10: all sound on ElevenLabs.
phases.gate: Budget: price one clip x every planned clip +about 30% retakes, check the balance right before submitting. Script Lab release 85+/100 with no critical fail. Hook stacks grade A or A+ on every channel. Voice never sped up more than 1.05x. A 15-second pilot is approved before the full VO.
phases.human_checkpoint: The user approves the 15 s pilot (hard gate 8) and picks the master hook stack at GATE 4 (hard gate 9).
phases.tools_models: MiniMax H3 2K, Kling 3.0 (fallback), Nano Banana 2, GPT Image 2, ElevenLabs connector

phases.name: Inputs
phases.does: Gathers the brand research (avatar, VOC, product truth, mechanism doc with UMP/UMS, offer) and the product URL. Notes every failed fix with its reason and every accommodation. Confirms the brand in one sentence with 2 to 3 findings and names the offer type (Section 0c).
phases.gate: With no research the URL is the minimum; with neither, stop. One ad = ONE avatar.

phases.name: Format, style, length, audio route
phases.does: Reads Appendix A first. Proposes 2 formats (from F1 to F13 or new), each with a reason and the 2 closest swipe ads. Picks a visual style: Pixar-style 3D, claymation, 2D flat or painterly, glossy 3D medical render, x-ray glass body on real footage, or mixed (a style skill such as claymation is used word for word). Sets the length tiers (a story tier, S60 or S90, plus a short tier, C45 or D30) and the audio route (narrator, character, dialogue, song, or text only).
phases.gate: No story under 55 s. L150 only with a stated reason. Final length is set by the measured voice pace, never by speeding the voice past 1.05x.
phases.human_checkpoint: GATE 2: format, style, tiers and audio route (line 133)

phases.name: Angle, awareness, mechanism picture
phases.does: ONE angle, ONE awareness stage, the narrator, and THE PICTURE: one visual metaphor of the mechanism, named as the UMP and repeated in the script.
phases.gate: The picture must pass the one-second read (7a) with no sound.

phases.name: Hook Lab
phases.does: Loads readymerce-hook-lab and runs H0 to H6. Checks the Hook Library (under 60 days old), generates stacks (visual, text, spoken, seam line), grades them, keeps 3 per format (a master and 2 variants, at least 2 hook types) and makes one concept frame per stack.
phases.gate: All 9 hook gates pass and every channel is A or A+ (A- is rewritten). Text hook 4 to 10 words; spoken sentence 1 is 8 to 14 words; problem in the first 6 words.
phases.tools_models: readymerce-hook-lab; Nano Banana 2 concept frames, about 2 credits each, checked at phone size with the text hook on top

phases.name: Scripts via Script Lab
phases.does: 4a: read Appendix A and the 2 closest swipe transcripts (curl in the Higgsfield sandbox). 4b: Script Lab WRITE with the brief card, the animation adapter, tiers, hook stacks and cast; the animation moves are mapped to rungs 0 to 13. 4c: format menu F1 to F13. 4d: voice script rules (words = tier seconds x pace; S/B/H gap codes; lines of 4 to 17 words; one line = one breath = one picture; IPA for the brand; brand named at least twice). 4e: the GATE 4 package (spine, MODELED ON, voice cast, hook stacks, visual idea) and, after the pick, the release per tier with supers and end card. 4f: 6 animation checks on each released script.
phases.gate: Script Lab release 85+/100 with no critical fail and cold readers (two from S90 up). Up to 3 rewrite loops, then the user decides. 4f: every line can be shown as one picture, carries a gap code and is TTS-safe.
phases.human_checkpoint: GATE 4: the user picks the spine and master hook stack plus 2 variants (line 235). Claude picks if told to run without stopping.
phases.tools_models: readymerce-script-lab; Higgsfield sandbox curl of the cloudfront transcripts

phases.name: Voice casting
phases.does: Writes a voice brief per speaker and shortlists 4 to 6 voices with creative_list_voices (or creative_design_voice). Auditions the hook and the mechanism-name line on eleven_v4 and eleven_v3 at 4 takes, scores the takes with vo_build2.py, then builds a 15 s pilot and calibrates the length from its measured WPM. Locks voice ID, model, tags and IPA.
phases.gate: Pilot approved before the full VO. If the script is more than about 10% over the tier, cut in Script Lab FIX or move up a tier. Never above 1.05x.
phases.human_checkpoint: The user picks the voice by ear and approves the pilot (part of GATE 5)
phases.tools_models: ElevenLabs creative_list_voices / creative_design_voice / creative_generate_speech (eleven_v4 default, eleven_v3 audition, multilingual_v2 for non-English, never turbo or flash)

phases.name: VO generation, scoring, master build
phases.does: Beats of 2 to 7 lines, one generate_speech call per beat, 4 takes, on one flow. Signed links are curled in the Higgsfield sandbox. vo_build2.py score reports words, pace (syll/s vs band), pitch movement and a score. vo_build2.py build cuts lines, trims, caps inner pauses at 0.4 s, joins lines with the S/B/H gaps, starts the first word at 0.03 s, normalizes to about -16 LUFS with peaks under -1.5 dB, and writes master.wav/mp3, vo_lines.csv and one stem per speaker. Uploads to Higgsfield.
phases.gate: Lowest score wins (10/word error + 3/syll-per-s outside the band + shortfall under 7 semitones + 1/flat line). A beat with no clean take is re-run with changed text. Never speed past 1.05x.
phases.human_checkpoint: The user approves the full VO master (GATE 5)
phases.tools_models: ElevenLabs; vo_build2.py v2.1 (remote cloudfront, praat-parselmouth, faster-whisper) in the Higgsfield sandbox

phases.name: Music bed and SFX
phases.does: Music on eleven_music_v2_5 with 2 takes, VO length +3 to 5 s, instrumental, mood by format. Mixed 14 to 18 dB under the voice with sidechain ducking; the bed drops out under the hook, turn, mechanism reveal and payoff; the beat grid comes from librosa. SFX on eleven_text_to_sound_v2 (0.5 to 30 s, prompt_influence 0.3), 4 takes, none under the hook words.
phases.gate: The user chooses the bed from rough mixes.
phases.human_checkpoint: GATE 5: voice (audition), then pilot, then full VO master and music bed (line 312)
phases.tools_models: ElevenLabs Music v2.5, ElevenLabs SFX v2, ffmpeg sidechaincompress, librosa

phases.name: Audio analysis (timing backbone)
phases.does: Word map with faster-whisper (medium.en or small.en) aligned to the script with difflib. Line table from vo_lines.csv plus each line's rung. Pause map. Report: length, WPM, first word, product shown and named as % of runtime, lines over 4 s, misheard words. VO slices for lip sync: stem cut from the sequence's first frame, 0.03 s fade, padded to whole seconds (max 15).
phases.gate: None numeric. Every shot later starts on a line start or a gap.

phases.name: Visual plan: 7a shot logic (12 tests), 7b shot ledger
phases.does: Picture changes every 2 to 4.5 s (median 3.5); 1 to 3 pictures in the first 5 s. Each shot is written as 'who does what to what, and what visibly changes'. The 12 tests: 1 one-second read; 2 cause and visible result in the same shot; 3 abstract lines need a contrast; 4 narrator asides set up the next idea; 5 real-world logic; 6 edit effects stay in the edit; 7 one panel = one moment = one state per character; 8 the prop that carries the line is exact; 9 the thing that carries the line is the subject; 10 a blocked or simplified shot must still carry its line; 11 inside-the-body shots are oriented; 12 a talking mouth is visible and the only one moving (face at least 1/3 of the frame). Ledger columns: Seq, Shot, Job, VO line, VO time, Sec, Mode (H3-REF / H3-KEY / KLING / STILL / REAL / CARD), Link (CHAIN/CUT), who/what, change, 1-second read, Pass. Sequences of up to 15 s with 2 to 4 shots; hold clips for key lines; shot counts per tier.
phases.gate: Only shots that pass every 7a test go to Phases 8 and 9.
phases.human_checkpoint: The ledger is shown at GATE 7

phases.name: Style bible, character bible, sheets
phases.does: 8a style bible: locked style block, closing line, motion guard, a palette of 4 to 6 colours (problem colour vs fix colour), negative list. 8b character bible. 8c sheets on Nano Banana 2 at 2K, in order: hero character, human character, group, product (label checked letter by letter), setting, inside-the-body, key prop. 8d state/variant sheets. 8e optional Higgsfield reference elements (H3 doesn't read elements). 8f reference order per step (H3: storyboard first, up to 9 images). 8g budget: usually 4 to 7 sheets. 8h consistency checks after every image and clip.
phases.gate: Each sheet checked at full size before the next. Nothing else is generated until the sheets pass.
phases.tools_models: Nano Banana 2 (2K); style skill (e.g. claymation) blocks

phases.name: Storyboard per sequence
phases.does: One image per sequence with the shots as panels: 2 to 3 shots = 16:9 canvas with 9:16 panels side by side; 4 shots = 4:5 canvas, 2x2. Thin white gutters, no text. Panels are frozen moments with characters counted. Storyboard check per panel: VO line | what a stranger reads in 1 s | pass or fail, plus clones, floating, props, subject size and mouth visible. The hook storyboard comes first and is checked at phone size with the text hook, sound off.
phases.gate: Any failed panel = regenerate that storyboard; a storyboard never goes to video without being looked at.
phases.human_checkpoint: GATE 7: storyboards plus the shot ledger, hook first; video only after approval (line 450)

phases.name: Video generation
phases.does: Model table: H3 reference mode (talking; up to 9 images + VO slice; 15 s max), H3 keyframe mode (non-talking; start and optional end frame), Kling 3.0 fallback (failed H3-KEY transformation), REAL (H3 from a GPT Image 2 iPhone-style still), STILL. 10a talking card: style block, references, timeline 'Shot N, a to b s', transitions, lip-sync block, camera, motion guard; 9:16 set explicitly; batch 2 on talking and hook sequences. Fallbacks: split the sequence into 2 clips, then keyframe + Sync Lipsync 3. 10b keyframe card: one action per clip, duration = VO span rounded up +about 0.5 s. 10c: NSFW rewrites re-run the 7a tests; budget preflight before every batch.
phases.gate: Sync verified by cross-correlating clip audio with the slice (should peak at 0 ms lag).
phases.tools_models: MiniMax H3 (2K), Kling 3.0, Sync Lipsync 3, GPT Image 2

phases.name: Deliverables before rendering
phases.does: Per sequence: ledger rows, the storyboard prompt with its ordered reference list, the video prompt or render card, the VO slices and fallback splits, the edit placement. Everything is saved to the project doc.

phases.name: Edit and assembly (Higgsfield sandbox)
phases.does: Pulls renders via show_generations. Frame check: one mid-shot frame per shot as contact sheets in a PDF viewed with pdf.js, running the 7a + 8h tests. Drift check: 2 s windows every 0.25 s; median offset if steps are under 0.15 s. Normalize to 1080x1920 at 30 fps (square clips cropped to 810x1440). VO master is the timeline; clips sped up to about 2.5x max. STILL zoompan 3 to 6%. Mix VO, then the ducked bed, then SFX; clip audio muted; fade the last second. Hook super (4 to 10 words, 0 to about 3 s, top). Captions with a 0.3 s tail, top 14% and bottom 20% clear. Supers of 2 to 6 words. End card (CTA, offer, guarantee, real product photo, fine print). Export 9:16 (+4:5).
phases.gate: Every failing shot is listed with its reason and retaken before the final edit. Retake for drift only when the drift sits inside a word. If frames can't be viewed, say so.

phases.name: QA
phases.does: Sound-off story check; hook check of the first 3 s at phone size; sound-on picture/line match; voice alone at phone volume; sheet match; lip sync only on the speaker; Copy Laws on screen; no generated text; model compliance (no Seedance or FLUX 3, Kling logged); Meta ad review risk (before/after); phone-size watch.
phases.gate: Pass/fail by inspection; first word at 0.0 s; problem in the first 6 words.

phases.name: Deliverable package
phases.does: Released scripts, voice cast, VO master, style and character bibles, sheet reference table, ledger, storyboards, render cards, the master and short tier, 3 hook stacks, primary text and headline, Script Lab releases, and credits spent vs the preflight.

story_structures.name: Belief-ladder spine (4b animation moves, rungs 0 to 13)
story_structures.shape: Hook (rung 0/1) > problem moments + accommodation (1-2) > failed fixes killed with a reason (3) > turn 'Here's what nobody told you' + named picture (4) > promise on a held shot (5) > mechanism in the picture's words, why fixes failed (6) > discovery, product shown before named, parts with jobs (7) > results timeline with honest dip + payoff callback + proof (8) > ease, offer, guarantee, urgency, CTA (9-12) > identity close (13)
story_structures.organic_fit: The skeleton for the 'POV day in the life, then the mechanism revealed' organic post. For an Albanian marketing agency: rungs 0 to 6 carry the post (the owner's week, their workarounds such as boosting posts and hiring a cousin to do Instagram, why each fails, the named cause such as 'the leaky funnel'). Rung 7 becomes 'what we do instead', shown as the method, not sold. Rungs 9 to 12 collapse into one organic CTA ('comment FUNNEL and I'll send you the checklist' / save / follow). Rung 13 identity close stays.

story_structures.name: Talking part ('I'm your...')
story_structures.shape: I am + symptom claim (0-5 s) > 3 symptoms 'every time you..., that's me' > fixes rebutted 'You think X fixes me? Wrong.' > what I really need > product shown, ingredient lines > results felt by the organ > proof > offer and guarantee > 'let me do my job' close
story_structures.organic_fit: Strong for organic comedy. A part of the business talks, in Albanian: 'I'm your Instagram inbox, and I've had 14 unanswered DMs since Friday.' It claims the symptoms, mocks the fixes and explains what it needs (a reply system or a content plan). Replace product/offer/guarantee with 'follow so your inbox stops crying' or 'send this to the person who runs your page'.

story_structures.name: Villain POV
story_structures.shape: Villain intro (0-4 s) > where it lives and what it does > fix 1, 2, 3 each mocked > 'you know what I'm actually scared of?' > product and its parts > villain losing its grip > offer > villain begs you not to click (close)
story_structures.organic_fit: Best comedic organic fit. Villains like the 'Boost Post' button, the agency that ghosts you, or the algorithm myth mock the owner's fixes, then admit what they fear: a consistent hook-first content system, the agency's method stated as a principle. Close: 'Please don't save this video.' That is a built-in save/share CTA with no price.

story_structures.name: Roll-call ('I am...')
story_structures.shape: Problem actors introduce themselves > solution actors (each step or deliverable) one job line each, one character per 5-8 s > squad line-up shot > 'most products send one of us, [brand] sends all four' > product
story_structures.organic_fit: Teach the agency's 3- or 4-step method as characters (the Hook, the Offer Post, the DM Reply, the Follow-up), each with one job line. Works as a save-worthy explainer at 30 to 45 s. Drop the competitor-comparison line or keep it soft; CTA 'save this before your next post'.

story_structures.name: 30-day timeline
story_structures.shape: Hook question (0-5 s) > day 1 nothing much, 'but here's what's already happening' > each stage: a felt change + the part doing it > day 30 identity line > brand, specs, offer, guarantee
story_structures.organic_fit: Services version from 0c: 'What happens in your first 30 days with us' (week 1 research dip, day 14 first win, day 30 result), or a habit timeline: 'What happens if you post one reel a day for 30 days.' For organic, keep the brand out of the hook (the card bans the brand in the first 3 s, but the F4 template names the product at 0-5 s). End with a 'follow for the day-30 results' series CTA. Numbers must be the agency's real case numbers.

story_structures.name: Anatomy / x-ray explainer
story_structures.shape: Hidden-cause hook with red top super (0-5 s) > 'this is a 3D render of...' > problem made visible and named > why it gets worse > what people try and why it can't reach it > the technology that reaches it > product > proof > guarantee > CTA
story_structures.organic_fit: The funnel as pipes, the ad account as a machine (0c): zoom into an Albanian shop's Instagram funnel and show where followers leak (no reply, no link, no offer post). A calm explainer that saves and shares well. Replace proof/guarantee/CTA with 'comment LEAK for the audit checklist' (feeds the DM funnel).

story_structures.name: One-character story (second/third person)
story_structures.shape: Narrated life of one character with the problem ('You are 65 years old...', 'A guy in his 30s running on bad sleep...'). Per the A3 beat map of ad 19: fear-moment hook > the accommodation > identity line > turn 'here is what nobody told you' + cause > failed fix killed > what the product does > timeline > proof/specs > urgency > guarantee + link
story_structures.organic_fit: This is the 'POV: a day in the life of the buyer' format. 'Arben runs a bakery in Durrës: up at 5, posts a blurry photo at 11, three likes, wonders why nobody orders.' It moves through his accommodations and the named hidden cause, then the payoff callback (the same bakery counter, now with a DM order). Close on identity; CTA follow/save. No offer, no urgency.

story_structures.name: Witness story
story_structures.shape: Surprising observation (0-5 s) > the secret habit > 'let me save you ten years of mistakes' lesson (the cause) > narrator tries it, honest first days > people notice > brand named late > offer > callback to the mentor
story_structures.organic_fit: Peer proof as story: 'The busiest restaurant in Tirana posts less than you do.' Then the habit (one hook-first reel a week, every DM answered in an hour), the lesson, the narrator trying it, people noticing. Brand is optional; drop the offer; callback close + 'follow for the next breakdown'. Must be a real, approved client or framed as an illustrative story.

story_structures.name: Personality reviewer
story_structures.shape: Sassy expert rates competitors one by one, then crowns the product (no beat map given beyond this)
story_structures.organic_fit: Organic version: a sassy animated strategist rates common marketing tactics out of 10 (buying followers 1/10, boosting random posts 3/10, giveaways 5/10, a hook-first reel series 9/10). Comments and debate drive reach. Don't name real competitors.

story_structures.name: Absurd metaphor hook
story_structures.shape: Cause shown as an impossible but instantly clear picture > plain explainer
story_structures.organic_fit: A shop owner pouring money into a bucket labelled 'Boost' with holes in the bottom, or a megaphone pointed at an empty field. One picture plus a 20 to 30 s explainer; strong first-frame hook for a short organic reel.

story_structures.name: Mixed media VSL
story_structures.shape: Realistic people/hands for problem and proof, 3D or 2D cutaways for the cause, product shots, customer montage
story_structures.organic_fit: For an agency, use the founder's or team's REAL face (filmed) for the hook and proof, with animation for the mechanism. Avoid AI-generated 'clients' or testimonials in organic posts; if any photoreal AI person appears, apply the platform AI label (this skill has no such rule).

story_structures.name: Text story
story_structures.shape: Long copy as on-screen text over one still or a slow loop, or one talking avatar
story_structures.organic_fit: Cheap organic filler: a short text story over a looping animated scene (for example the bakery inbox). Keep it to 15 to 30 s with 1 to 3 words per caption card; works without a voiceover budget. CTA 'send this to a business owner friend'.

story_structures.name: Flat 2D explainer
story_structures.shape: Vector or painterly illustration, narrator, step-by-step how to use
story_structures.organic_fit: A 3-step how-to ('How to answer a price DM in Albanian without losing the sale'), save-bait at 20 to 40 s, in a consistent flat brand style that becomes the client's recurring look.

story_structures.name: Song (route to readymerce-song-ads)

story_structures.name: Short tier: conversation or problem demo
story_structures.shape: 40 to 50 s conversation or problem demo, never a cut-down story (Script Lab section 10)
story_structures.organic_fit: Two animated characters (owner and strategist) in a 30 to 45 s dialogue: the owner's objection, a one-line reframe, a quick demo. Good native organic length; CTA 'comment the word X'.

story_structures.organic_fit: All carry to organic B2B with service nouns: 'Stop boosting posts if you sell in Tirana', 'This is why your reels get 200 views', 'I'm your unanswered DM'. Keep the card's rule: no brand, price or offer in the first 3 s.

visual_qa_overlap:
ALREADY IN THE SKILL:
(1) Shot-level design QA before any image: the 12 shot-logic tests in 7a, and the 7b ledger columns '1-second read' and 'Pass' ('Only shots that pass every 7a test go to Phase 8 and 9').
(2) Sheets: each of the 7 sheet types is 'checked at full size before the next' (8c). The product label is checked 'letter by letter'. The 8h consistency checks (face, signature details, outfit, squad order and size, single readable label, no clones or floating, prop readings) run 'after every image and every clip'. GATE 6 is human approval of every sheet.
(3) Storyboards: a per-panel table 'VO line | what a stranger reads in 1 second | pass or fail' plus counts (no clones, nobody floats, props match their sheets, the subject is big enough, the mouth is visible). The hook storyboard is checked first at phone size with the text hook, sound off. GATE 7 is human approval.
(4) Prompt cards: 10a says every H3 prompt 'follows the hub G1 prompt card' and gives a 7-part structure. 10b is a keyframe render card. 8f fixes the reference order. Phase 11 hands over storyboard and video prompts with ordered reference lists. Retakes 'change one thing in the prompt'.
(5) Takes: 10a sync check by cross-correlation (0 ms lag). Phase 12 step 2 frame check: one mid-shot frame per shot, contact sheets in a PDF viewed via pdf.js, the 7a + 8h tests, and failing shots listed with fixes. Phase 12 step 3 drift check (2 s windows / 0.25 s). Phase 13 QA (sound off, hook at phone size, lip sync only on the speaker, no generated text).

WEAKNESSES A FRESH-AGENT REVIEWER WOULD FIX:
(a) Every check is run by the same agent that wrote the prompts and picked the takes. This is the self-grading failure the skill already fixed for scripts with a cold reader (lesson line 556), and it has not been applied to visuals. A fresh Visual Reviewer given only the shot ledger row (line, 'who does what to what', expected 1-second read) and the image would replace the self-run storyboard check and the Phase 12 step 2 frame check with an independent pass/fail.
(b) There is no prompt linter. The 10a structure claims to follow the hub G1 card, but it omits the card's 'hands and props line' and 'background line in every shot'. Those are the exact causes of the vanished phone and the frozen room in lesson line 550. It also never mentions declined_preset_id, the 5 s minimum duration or whole-second durations. A Prompt Reviewer would check every card before spend: all G1 parts present, style block + closing line + motion guard verbatim, 9:16 and 2K, duration whole seconds within 5 to 15, reference tokens matching upload order, one action per shot, no edit effects in the prompt (7a test 6), character count stated.
(c) Frame sampling is thin: one frame from the middle of each shot misses mid-clip morphs, vanishing props, cuts H3 skipped and end-of-clip drift. A Take Reviewer should sample several frames per shot (start/mid/end or every 0.5 to 1 s, plus crops of faces, hands, labels and mouths). It should add OCR for generated text and label drift, count characters per frame for clones, check lip motion only in the speaker's region, and report numeric drift results.
(d) There are no numeric pass thresholds or retake caps for visuals (only 'Retake only when the drift sits inside a word' and a +30% budget). Reviewers need explicit thresholds and a max-retakes-per-shot rule that escalates to a human.
(e) There is no GATE after the final edit; Phase 13 QA is self-run. A final fresh-agent review against the ledger and Copy-Law checklist before the hub draft would cover it.
(f) The 7a tests only run as self-review at storyboard time. Reviewers could apply them twice: to the written ledger (design) and to the rendered take (execution).
